title: Exclusive — President of Cyprus: ‘Sky Is the Limit’ for Bilateral Relations with USA
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Exclusive — President of Cyprus: ‘Sky Is the Limit’ for Bilateral Relations with USA, Trump Has ‘Unique Advantage’ in Negotiations Because ‘You Know Where You Stand’ with POTUS

NEW YORK — President of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides told Breitbart News exclusively on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly that American President Donald Trump has a “unique advantage” in world affairs.
The post Exclusive — President of Cyprus: ‘Sky Is the Limit’ for Bilateral Relations with USA, Trump Has ‘Unique Advantage’ in Negotiations Because ‘You Know Where You Stand’ with POTUS appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
NEW YORK — President of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides told Breitbart News exclusively on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) that American President Donald Trump has a “unique advantage” in world affairs because, while he is bold, everyone knows where they are in his book, which helps him negotiate better than anyone.

“For me, President Trump has a unique advantage,” Christodoulides told Breitbart News during a nearly hourlong exclusive interview in late September here at the UNGA. “Either you like it or not, but you know where you stand. When you know where you stand, you can sit together, discuss, and even in the most challenging and difficult issues, find a solution. He proves that we may disagree, but if we sit together, we can find the solution.”

Christodoulides’s comments on Trump came during a broader part of the interview focused on how Cyprus just wrapped its rotating presidency of the European Union’s council earlier this year, and how he sought to bring Europe closer both with the Eastern Mediterranean and Middle East but also with the United States. He argued that Europe does not “have the luxury” to not stand shoulder-to-shoulder alongside Trump and the United States, and that Western civilization needs the West actually unified.

Breitbart News Washington Bureau Chief Matthew Boyle, right, interviews President of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. (Office of the President of Cyprus)

“The number one highlight of our presidency was to bring the region closer to the European Union,” Christodoulides said. “It took a lot of time and effort in order to make my colleagues, the European Council, understand the importance of the greater Middle East, and we are very glad. Within this context, we also had an informal meeting in Cyprus with the 27 member states; the leaders of the 27 member states, and the presidents of the institutions with leaders of the region. The second one is the importance that we attach finally as a European Union on the issue of defense. We are spending through the SAFE instrument 150 billion euros in order to enhance the capabilities of the European Union and the member states. The third point, which is very very important for us, in certain issues, is we may have different approaches with the United States, but we don’t have the luxury in any way to have a transatlantic rift.”

Trump’s new ambassador to Cyprus, John Breslow, just took office earlier in September, and Christodoulides told Breitbart News he has hit the ground running there already.

“The new ambassador was in several places working last week,” Christodoulides said in the interview, conducted the week of the high-level UNGA gatherings in New York City in late September.

“The United States is our most important partner in trade, defense, and security in all sectors,” Christodoulides said. “As I told you, one of the reasons that the European Union actually today exists is because of the support of the United States back immediately after World War II, and we don’t have the luxury to have a transatlantic rift. We need to work together, and it was very important. I mentioned this before that finally, as a European, for a number of years, I remember when I was Minister of Foreign Affairs or before a government spokesman or diplomatic adviser of the former president, we were discussing about the need to enhance our defense capability. Discussion, discussion, just discussion, and very nice declarations, very nice conclusions. It’s the first time that we decided very, very specifically, to spend 150 billion euros in order to enhance our defense and security capabilities, and Cyprus will be benefited out of this instrument with 1.2 billion euros in order to enhance our defense capability.
